_about: What the hooks research says works now, boiled down per surface, so every title round starts from it. Source: docs/research/2026-10-14-viral-hooks-corpus.md (Krish shared it on 2026-10-14: 'Here is some research you can build a better hook generation system from ... commit this knowledge so you can tap it as required'). Krish's own picks in config/title-verdicts.json win wherever the two disagree. Printed by `title_check.py lessons --surface <surface>`. On 2026-10-17 Krish attached his own playbook (docs/research/2026-10-17-ai-hook-title-thumbnail-playbook.md, "The AI Future: Hook, Title, & Thumbnail Playbook"), straight after rejecting a round of headings and asking what a Substack headline is next to the Substack cover and a YouTube thumbnail. Its formulas sit under each surface as "krish_playbook" and win over the research where the two differ. Two house rules still hold over it: a line must be true to the piece (title_check's source check; never over-claim), and its fear and urgency (IT'S OVER, TOO LATE) belong to packaging only: the titles, thumbnails and opening hooks, never the script or the article body (house rule REFLECTIVE_VOICE).
formula: Specific subject + visible stakes + proof marker + one honest open loop, inside the surface's first readable space, with the words people search for early, and the payoff delivered fast.
everywhere: Name the subject: a person, product, company, number or moment. Vague curiosity is losing to specific, honest tension.
Keep one honest open loop and pay it off early in the piece (YouTube: in the first 5 to 10 seconds). Over-promising is now punished after the click.
First person ('I tried', 'I scored') is the strongest tested opener (+19% within the same creator on LinkedIn).
Stack three or four frames into one idea (action + constraint + stake), not one buzzword.
A proof marker makes the promise believable: a number, a duration, a sample size.

Slop tells to kill: 'it's not X, it's Y', 'Unpopular opinion:', 'Let that sink in.', rule-of-three filler, stacked rhetorical questions. Test: delete the name; if nobody could tell it was Krish's, it is slop.
Never over-claim. A misleading title wins the click and loses the trust.

youtube.formula: [stacked story frame] + [specific number or name] + [stake]. The thumbnail completes the title; it never repeats it.
strong: tenure: I've done X for N years (>2x)
contradiction ('..., but nobody will buy it')

shorts.formula: Title = the words people search + a specific outcome (30 to 50 characters). First frame shows motion and the payoff object; on-screen text is a 3 to 7 word claim. Caption every spoken hook: most watch muted.
strong: 'what nobody tells you' (transferred across every niche)

cover.formula: 3 to 5 big words that complete the title, not repeat it; a contradiction or a reveal ('You've been lied to').
strong: one face with clear emotion (+18 to 32%)

card.formula: A 3 to 7 word claim the picture proves; named subject, surprise last.
weak: a label or a topic heading

article.formula: On Substack the title is also the email subject and the homepage headline: under about 60 characters, with a specific number, a broken rule, or an unexpected word in an expected phrase. The subtitle (60 to 150 characters) says who it is for and what they walk away with.
strong: a resource readers can save or forward
weak: describing the topic instead of the reader's situation

linkedin.formula: I + [specific decision or moment] + [unexpected consequence] + [unresolved why], with the topic keyword in line one.
weak: 'you' address (-10%) unless the reader is the subject

blog.formula: [main search phrase in the first 3 words] + [checkable claim or number] + [something an AI summary can't give: data, a template, tested, first-hand]. Match the H1.
strong: a number kept in title and H1

thumbnail.formula: Under 4 words over his face and the logos, completing the YouTube title, never repeating it.

opening.formula: The first 5 seconds on camera, or the article's first paragraph: keep them once they have clicked.
strong: the payoff of the title in the first 5 to 10 seconds

surface_map.article: The Substack headline: the post's title, also the email subject line and the homepage headline. Words only.
surface_map.subtitle: The Substack subtitle under the headline (also the email preview line). Words only.
surface_map.cover: The Substack cover image: the picture at the top of the post and on social cards, with his face and 3 to 5 big words. It completes the headline, never repeats it. The YouTube thumbnail shares its words and look when both fit.
surface_map.youtube: The YouTube title of the long cut, and the Substack video post's title (it starts "VIDEO:" there, and that post is also the email subject).
surface_map.thumbnail: The YouTube thumbnail of the long cut (wide, 16:9): his face, the companies' logos, under 4 words that complete the YouTube title, never repeat it.
surface_map.shorts: The title of the 90-second cut on YouTube Shorts, and the caption's first line on TikTok and Instagram Reels.
surface_map.tall_cover: The 90-second cut's cover frame (tall, 9:16): the frame the Shorts, TikTok and Reels grids show, with under 4 words.
surface_map.title_card: The title card inside both videos, in the story intro: the video's own name, short (60 characters at most).
surface_map.card: A heading on a picture that cuts in while he talks: a line a viewer reads in a second, from what he is saying at that moment.
surface_map.opening: The first 5 seconds he says on camera (the hook), and the first paragraph of the article.

krish_playbook.psychology: FOMO, urgency, authority and curiosity gaps

formulas.name: The Time Bomb
examples: AI in 2027: Why 90% of White-Collar Jobs Are Changing Today
The Next 6 Months in AI Will Break the Internet
AGI is Coming in 2025 (And We Are Not Ready)

formulas.name: The Secret/Leak
examples: The OpenAI Leak That Proves GPT-5 is Already Here
What Sam Altman Isn't Telling You About the Next AI Wave

formulas.name: The Paradigm Shift
formulas.structure: The End of [Current Tech/Status Quo] (Enter [New AI])
examples: Prompt Engineering is Dead. This is What's Next.
Forget ChatGPT: Autonomous AI Agents Are the Real Threat

youtube.rule: Punchy, emotional, broad enough for a wide audience, promising insider knowledge.

formulas.name: Doomsday/Ominous
formulas.structure: dark, moody; a company logo glowing, cracked or glitching
examples: IT'S OVER.
TOO LATE.

formulas.name: Graph/Chart of Doom
formulas.structure: a line shooting up off the screen; Krish in front, shocked or pointing at the turn
examples: EXPONENTIAL.

formulas.name: Forbidden Document
formulas.structure: a blurred "top secret" page or a glowing screen, one shocking word readable
examples: LEAKED.
DON'T LOOK.

thumbnail.rule: Never repeat the title: give a visual curiosity gap. Text under 4 words.

formulas.name: The Contrarian Thesis
formulas.structure: Why [Popular Opinion] is Wrong, and [Your AI Prediction] is Right
examples: Why the "AI Bubble" Isn't Bursting. It's Mutating.
Stop Worrying About Superintelligence. Worry About Autonomous Swarms.

formulas.name: The Deep Dive Briefing
examples: The Executive's Guide to Post-LLM Architecture.
What Happens When AI Models Start Training Themselves? A Deep Dive.

formulas.name: The Urgent Trend
formulas.structure: [New AI Trend] is Here. Here's How to Prepare.
examples: The Shift from Chatbots to Action-Bots has Begun.
Why 'Compute' is the New Oil: The Geopolitics of Future AI.

article.rule: Less clickbait than YouTube, still compelling: depth, analysis and authority, a perspective of his own.

formulas.name: YouTube (visual and fast)
formulas.structure: what everyone is distracted by, then what is really happening, then when it lands
examples: Everyone is distracted by ChatGPT right now. But buried deep in a new research paper last night, researchers just unlocked the technology that makes ChatGPT look like a pocket calculator. And it's rolling out next month.

formulas.name: Substack (analytical)
formulas.structure: the misunderstanding, the real shift happening quietly, then "let's unpack the timeline"
examples: There is a fundamental misunderstanding about where AI is heading in the next 18 months. ... Let's unpack the timeline.

opening.rule: You have 5 seconds to keep them once they click.
